questions.text: What does "multimodal" mean when describing an AI system?

options.text: The AI can be used by several people at the same time.
The AI works with several types of data — text, images, audio and video.
The AI can be switched between different personalities.
The AI runs on several computers at once.

questions.explanation: "Multimodal" simply means multiple modes of information — much as a teacher combines a whiteboard drawing, a verbal explanation and a hands-on activity in one lesson.

questions.text: Because multimodal AI can actually see an image, its visual analysis does not need to be verified.
questions.explanation: The same caution applies as with text: the model recognises patterns, not meaning, and can misidentify objects, misread handwriting or misinterpret context — so visual analysis should always be checked, especially in assessment.

questions.text: Which limitations of multimodal AI does the lesson list?

options.text: Accuracy is not guaranteed — it can misidentify objects or generate images with errors.
Bias in training data can produce stereotypical representations of people or professions.
It cannot process written text at all.
Copyright and attribution questions around generated images are still unresolved.
Uploading photographs of students raises privacy concerns.

questions.explanation: Accuracy, bias, copyright, the irreplaceable value of real observation and privacy are all named as limitations; working with text remains a core capability, not a limitation.

questions.text: Which multimodal feature does the lesson suggest trying first?

options.text: Generating a full video for a lesson.
Uploading a single image and asking a question about it.

questions.explanation: The lesson advises starting simple: uploading one image and asking a question about it reveals both the power and the limits of multimodal AI in a way that is immediately useful.
